one_liner: Vonage offers self-serve communications APIs (SMS, Voice, Messages, Verify, etc.) with API key/secret and JWT auth, free signup credit, and official MCP servers.
auth_notes: Main APIs use account API key/secret (Basic header) or JWTs signed with an application's private key. OAuth2 applies only to the gated Vonage Business Communications APIs and CAMARA network APIs. There is no multi-user OAuth for the core APIs, so the toolkit takes per-customer credentials.
access_notes: Free signup gives an API key and secret plus €2 test credit in DEMO mode (limited to 10 destination numbers). Production use needs paid credit. VBC APIs require 50+ extensions and a CSM. RCS requires managed-customer onboarding.
blocker_notes: Signup is self-serve and free. Credentials are per-account (key/secret or JWT) rather than OAuth. Demo mode limits sending until credit is added.

evidence.quote: Basic Authentication sends your API Key and API Secret **Base64-encoded** in the `Authorization` header.
Vonage APIs (Voice, Messages, Conversation, etc) use JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) for authentication. JWTs must be signed with the private key of your application.
When you create your Vonage account you are given €2 free test credit and your account is set in DEMO mode.
Ensure your organization has 50 extensions or more.
Messages supports both JWT and Basic authentication, however basic authentication does not support webhooks or advanced features such as ACLs.
The Vonage MCP Server allows AI agents and developer tools to interact with Vonage APIs through the Model Context Protocol
also known as the Tooling MCP Server, lets you invoke various API actions directly through your LLM Assistant or IDE of choice.
